environment.hardware: MacBook Pro Mac17,6, Apple M5 Max, 128 GB

calibration.basis: Owner decision 2026-10-06 (plan 0012), replacing the 2026-10-04 validity rule. Performance gates measure the machine's natural idle state. On a quiet, cool Mac on AC, the probe read 1.45-2.05 ms with nothing else running and 1.16-1.22 ms with one other core busy: the CPU stays clocked down for bursty work, so a slow loop is the idle state the user meets, not an invalid run. A warm run under the old rule was invalid on 45 of 45 attempts at a 1-minute load of 1.3-3.8. The reference is the fast-state p50 measured 2-4 October (about 60 warm runs of our build and upstream at a load of 2.4-5.3), kept as context for the recorded loop times.
calibration.rule: Every warm, upstream and installed run records the calibration loop's p50 and p90 (the keyup loop, or the probe for a fresh-application observation) as information beside its results. The loop never makes a run invalid, never reruns it and never leaves it inconclusive for a slow CPU: every run is scored against the unchanged thresholds, for our build and upstream alike. Runs still require AC power, an open lid, nice 0 and a 1-minute load below 6.

sampling.scenarios: Run every Phase 1A scenario on every representative document; report each distribution separately without pooling documents. Start a fresh application with a fresh profile for every observation. Run all warmup rounds before measured rounds in deterministic rotating round-robin order; execute every representative document once per round and rotate the first document by one position continuously across round and phase boundaries. The authenticated launcher starts runner-owned caffeinate display sleep prevention before package build and holds it through sampling and cleanup; it does not synthesize input or focus the app. Before pre-timing readiness, Electron calls setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, { visibleOnFullScreen: true, skipTransformProcessType: true }); readiness asserts isVisibleOnAllWorkspaces() === true and isHiddenInMissionControl() === true. Pre-timing readiness requires two consecutive exact Electron and CGWindow matches within a bounded 5 seconds. During pre-timing readiness only, a transient origin mismatch or missing optional onScreen metadata on the otherwise exact CGWindow row may settle, but readiness cannot complete until the external CGWindow row provides explicit on-screen proof; explicit onScreen false remains strict and fails immediately. Post-measurement validation remains one-shot strict, and null onScreen metadata remains strict there. Cleanup reverses the workspace policy with setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(false, { visibleOnFullScreen: false, skipTransformProcessType: true }) before restoring window state. Application launch and readiness are excluded from metrics; the window remains unfocused and not always-on-top, with no retries. This deterministic rotating round-robin limits fixed document/time-order confounding but does not eliminate temporal, thermal, or environment drift. Report mandatory time-ordered drift diagnostics for every document and metric; no pass/fail threshold is defined before owner ratification. Application close and profile cleanup occur outside every timed metric.

t_event.definition: Browser beforeinput timestamp; trace origin, not physical-input time.

t_echo.definition: Elapsed time from t_event to the exact speculative DOM checkpoint.

t_dispatch.definition: Elapsed time from t_event until the edit transaction is dispatched to the authority actor.

t_ack.definition: Elapsed time from t_event until the authority actor acknowledges the transaction.

t_reconcile.definition: Elapsed time from t_event until authoritative reconciliation completes.

t_present.definition: Elapsed time from t_event through Electron WebContents.capturePage with stayHidden and stayAwake after the exact acknowledged view checkpoint in the transparent, render-active, inactive macOS measurement window, followed by immediate retained-state validation; a captured compositor-surface upper bound, not proof of pixel equality, physical display, vsync, or next-frame time.

open.definition: Elapsed time from the open request until the authoritative document session is accepted.

first_viewport.definition: Elapsed time from the open request until the first viewport is editable.
